processing: Nothing specific is documented; Phoenix dancong is generally sun-withered, shaken and rested in rounds, then fixed, rolled and dried.
harvest_season: Not documented; spring is the main picking for Phoenix dancong in general.
appearance_dry: Not specifically described; dancong in general is long, twisted and dark brown.
appearance_liquor: Not specifically described; dancong liquor is usually clear golden to light amber.
appearance_wet: Not specifically described; dancong leaves usually show reddened edges after shaking.
taste_profile: No agreed description exists, because the line is filed under different aroma types: ginger-flower in one account, cinnamon or miscellaneous clear-fragrance in another.

brewing.notes: General dancong approach only: very hot water and quick pours.

vintage_note: No selling pattern is documented for this line. Phoenix dancong is usually sold by spring harvest of the current year, sometimes with older roasted stock marked by year. Since the name describes a leaf rather than a scent, ask which aroma a given lot is meant to have.
description:
Shan Qie Ye, 'mountain eggplant leaf', is a Phoenix dancong named for the shape of its leaf rather than its scent, like Yang Mei Ye or Zhu Ye. That is the firmest thing known about it.

Its aroma is less settled. A Chinese overview lists it among representative ginger-flower lines, while a vendor's list of Phoenix trees gives a Shan Qie Ye Rou Gui Xiang and other Shan Qie Ye trees in its clear-fragrance group. Leaf-shape names can cover more than one tree, which may explain this.

Its processing and cup aren't specifically described, so treat it as typical dancong: expect a shaken, partly oxidised leaf, and brew it hot and quick. Let your own tasting decide what family it belongs to.

When buying, the seller's description of aroma and village tells you more than the name does.
history: No date or person is documented for this line. A Chinese tea science overview lists the name among trees named by leaf shape. One vendor's list places Shan Qie Ye trees in Da'an and Zimao Dingcuo, Fengxi Village, and gives the Da'an mother tree as about 200 years old at about 900 to 950 m; those are a seller's figures.
